_comment: Predictions written BEFORE any engine was run, from each engine's documented semantics and from reading the policy sources. A mismatch with observed results is a finding to explain, not a value to overwrite. psa = Pod Security Admission 'restricted' (live); vap = lab-pod-extra-controls ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (live); kyverno = existing policies/hardened-pods.yaml via `kyverno test` (offline); opa = policies/rego/workload.rego (offline). History: the first prediction for compliant-app, compliant-api-reader, gap-latest-tag and gap-projected-token-unapproved was kyverno=pass. The Kyverno CLI returned fail for all four. Diagnosis (confirmed by re-running with ONLY container-level runAsNonRoot added): policies/hardened-pods.yaml reads runAsNonRoot at container level only, so a pod that sets it at pod level - which PSA treats as compliant - is rejected. The corpus pods now set it at both levels, and finding-pod-level-only-run-as-non-root pins the false positive. The existing policy was not modified. Second miss: the live combined PSA+VAP result for gap-automounted-token differed from the VAP-only result because lab-hardened's ServiceAccount sets automountServiceAccountToken=false while the ServiceAccount first created in lab-vap-only used defaults, so a pod that merely omitted the field was protected only in lab-hardened. The case now sets the field explicitly, both namespaces use the same ServiceAccount definitions, and finding-sa-level-automount-false pins the evaluation-context difference (offline engines read the Pod alone and treat omission as true).
